text_fidelity_a:
Hygge Games How did You Know That? – Trivia Party Game, White As a lover of board games… Our family members each receive a new addition to the game closet in their stocking every year… With kids off to college- I am constantly looking for new and fun options that don’t take a lot explaining or, learning and can peek their interest, liking them to be a bit competitive yet, can be played with minimal effort- So, a hard combo to find! So, I’m happy to say… “How did You know That-“ falls into this category!!

DID YOU KNOW THAT is easy enough to learn and that’s a perk! Also, a big plus is the fact, it’s easy to explain it to those who have a tendency to not pay attention during rule reading (we all know a few of “those type” people- ha ha..!!) BUT, with an easy concept they’ll be playing like pros in no time.. LOVE the fact, this game can be tweaked and adapted if necessary.. and we always love those! (Anything that allows you to simplify or shorten a game as needed.. is like sprinkles on top!)

Basic idea: one person reads 4 questions in a row off of x1 card. All other players write their 4 answers down… THEN, players will correct answers as revealed for all 4 questions asked. giving x1 pt. per correct answer. If only x1 person gets it right the crowd shouts “how did you know that!” and gets double points. Its that simple..

This is full of Quirky odd questions at various levels of some useful/not trivia! Winner is whoever has most points at the end of game..
Best part is: YOU decide do you play to a certain point level (1st one to 10, 20 wins?) OR, do you give everyone certain amount of cards so, everyone has a turn or two to read questions.. if so then, at the end of all reveals.. they tally up those points received to see who’s the winner! That’s it..!!!

This would make a great game for the dorms- (especially during the time of the pandemic.. these kids have a lot of Shelter in place/quarantine time!) for those old enough, I could see it turning this into a drinking game of sorts (good or, bad?!) it would easily adapt.
Definitely, feel this is geared toward older teens or, adults.. it’s too hard for younger kids. I do feel this has a niché for academics and know it alls! Any with mega time spent learning, reading, gaining random facts off the Internet- it’s a great way to share that trivial academia skills.. Ha! Some things will just be fun facts you picked up thru life, in elementary school or, info. From those who’ve raised you.. tossed with real trivia facts. So, the smartest person doesn’t always win!? Fun for a competitive group with a plethora of knowledge and facts to share!!
Played with our college kids over holiday and it went back to the dorm bc, of its fun factor- with x3 college kids and/or, recent graduates.. we had a ball! I hope this info can help your decision.. feel free to let me know!
text_fidelity_b: Hygge Games How did You Know That? – Trivia Party Game, White

LEGO Creator 3in1 Twin Rotor Helicopter 31096 Building Kit (569 Pieces) This is a great quality play set with hundreds of pieces that will keep your kids occupied for hours. The box says 569 pieces, which is enough to build a lot of different objects.

As a parent, it's not hard to see the advantage of Lego sets. Although I think it's a little ridiculous to assume that your kid will grow up to be an engineer if they play with Legos, it's easy to see the benefit of a toy that makes children follow rigorous and complex instructions.

The build diagrams are a lot like you will encounter on any number of products in your lifetime, for everything from maintaining your vacuum cleaner, to the owner's manual of your vehicle, to how to put on a compression valve. The early you learn how to sit down and interpret an instructional diagram, the better equipped you are to deal with life.

The most amazing thing about Lego sets is that even though they are a rigorous mental exercise, kids love digging into them each and every time. This set is triple the fun as it contains the instructions for three different builds. My kids are 7 and 9 and they put together the boat in a couple hours. The boat even has a mechanism that allows you to spin a handle on the top and it makes the propeller spin (although we couldn't quite get the piece to set in place properly). Still, this is a complex build that gives a little bit of insight into gearing.

The best part is, once they're done building all the suggestions, they break the whole thing down and start constructing fortresses and whatnot. I have never seen a kid disappointed to receive a Lego set ever. Great toy.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator 3in1 Twin Rotor Helicopter 31096 Building Kit (569 Pieces)

The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games I'm a wolf lover as well as a game nerd and couldn't pass this one up! It is absolutely beautiful out of the box. I'm impressed they kept it to a $50 price point with the level of detail here, I've seen similar games priced closer to $80!

I haven't had a chance to play yet because I need to get folks together but I did watch a video playthrough about the rules after reading the guide so that I'd be prepared. They are complex but once I watched the video it made a lot more sense. It's definitely tactic-heavy in that you need to change strategy based on what your opponent is doing or what phase of the moon it is on. I love many of the creative points in the design, and I love a game with a very clear endpoint because I hate games that go on forever! 75 minutes is perfect for a game night.

I especially love the design of the wolf cards. They are extremely clear where the tiles and meeples go etc. It's not only attractive but it also includes reminder text which is really helpful for absent-minded players like myself. I love how the rules for your items level up as you get more pieces on the board.

My favorite part about games like this is that it's possible to lose a battle here and there and not feel discouraged halfway through. Since a lot of scoring can happen later, it keeps players invested until the end. This generation of games is so different from the ones before!

My only complaint is that with a game like this it is so easy to lose a meeple because they are so small and so many. This can make it hard to trust strangers with at board-game meetups.
text_fidelity_b: The Wolves Board Game | Wolf Themed Survival Strategy Game | Highly Interactive Family Game for Kids and Adults | Ages 14+ | 2-5 Players | Avg. Playtime 75 Minutes | Made by Pandasaurus Games

TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+ When I was in high school my senior class played an elimination game that was vaguely similar to this (and has been around for years and is still played across the country). Each person drew a name and that was the "target", and there were only loose rules on how to "eliminate" your target (most memorable weapon was a seltzer bottle), and graduation was the time limit. TAG is basically a formalization of that game, with fewer players and more specifics on elimination.

My graduating class had over 500 people, and not all of them played the game. Still, with 50+ players and months to play, it was unwieldy then. TAG limits the game to 10 players max, and the time frame can span anywhere from an hour or two to several weeks. Though the rules are flexible enough to allow for playing for months, this gets a bit cumbersome when having a small player pool.

Each player gets an ID card ("credentials") and a target name. Unlike the more informal version of the game, players are given specific instructions on how to eliminate their target. It might be luring the target to a location or lying in wait, getting the target to do something, or more. Nailing the target with the squirt gun or "poisoning" their food with salt might be fun but if it's not on the specific method card, it doesn't count. Once you've eliminated your target, your next target becomes whoever your original target was stalking. Gameplay continues until there's only one player left.

I like the way this game refines the elimination process, and I like the smaller, more limited scope. This makes it a good game for family events, fun in the dorms at school or even a company morale booster.

If you've ever played the old elimination game, this will be familiar territory. If you haven't it's a fun introduction. There's reasonably good replayability and there's enough flexibility to either play quickly or draw it out for days and weeks.
text_fidelity_b: TAG -- Live-Action Elimination Competition -- Eliminate Your Target Until You're The Last One Standing -- 4-10 Players -- Ages 14+

text_fidelity_a:
HOT WHEELS MONSTER TRUCKS MECHA SHARK FACE-OFF Play Set Once we unboxed the Hot Wheels Monster Trucks Mecha Shark Face-off Playset my 6 year old has been launching cars and trucks for about two hours now.

Hot Wheels is often hit or miss. They sometimes have a great idea and an awesomely executed toy. Sometimes the toy created nothing but frustration. So, this playset has captured my son's imagination and interest for a couple hours now.

The idea is that this is a Monster Truck Arena and you are to launch your Monster Truck into another Truck that is placed in a trophy. When you do so, there is a shark that spins and it spins to catch/eat/collect the Truck kicked out the trophy while your truck has landed in the trophy. I think.

Set-up as far as Hot Wheels goes was pretty easy. It took me a total of about 20 minutes to put it together plus the stickers (ugh!). This part of the instructions has no words so you have to guess. Be extra careful to peel the stickers off and put them on! (Any parents know that the worst part are the stickers!!) But once you have the base and the stickers on the base, the rest goes pretty fast and your kid is ready to launch. This comes with two Monster Trucks. One of the Trucks "falls apart" as if it's been actually in a crash. There are two spaces to put extra cars or Monster Trucks. You can play with just one person or with two people vying to try to land inside the trophy.

This is stand alone playset. It does not attach to any other Hot Wheel set. In other words there are no tracks to go with this set. And I'm ok with that. The reason for 3 stars instead of 4 is that I'm scared for the shark mechanism. I have a feeling that it will someone stop spinning or that my son will push in the wrong direction too many times and it will break. Actually, based on my experience, I know that will happen, it's just a matter of how soon that will occur. On the first day or in a couple days time. I would say that the instructions on how to play were confusing and didn't really make any sense. So, my description on what to do is based on what my son said and my interpretation of what the toy looks like.

Overall, my son spent hours launching cars into the air. He couldn't be happier and that makes me happy.

UPDATE:
As predicted (within 24 hours) something was bound to break. One of the Monster Truck launchers stopped retracting back so its ability to launch a truck as high or fast is greatly diminished. Therefore, playing with this playset isn't as fun as it used to be.
text_fidelity_b: HOT WHEELS MONSTER TRUCKS MECHA SHARK FACE-OFF Play Set

Snap Circuits Classic SC-300 Electronics Exploration Kit | Over 300 Projects | Full Color Manual Parts | STEM Educational Toy for Kids 8+ 2.3 x 13.6 x 19.3 inches I got this kit for my 10 year old. We had been experimenting with kit electric motors, magnets and radios and everything ended up mixed in a box that he liked to play with, so there was interest in this type of toy.

The parts of this kit snap together on a clear plastic grid. The instruction book is a black and white center stapled pamphlet that can be challenging to decipher for builds that are more complex. My son liked building the simple circuit that included the motor with the fan. Many of the advanced plans are very similar.

The kit seems durable but not indestructable. My kids can be pretty rough on things so they have been using this kit with my supervision.

For most kids under 10, this is not the type of toy that they can play with on their own. I have my son use this toy at the dining room table. We check to make sure that all of the parts get back in their place when we are done.

This is an educational toy. My experience is that early exposure to learning experiences like this can shape interests later on in life.

I would have liked to have seen a description of what the various modules do to the electricity to make the magic happen.

If you have any specific questions please leave a comment and I'll try to get back to you as soon as I can.

Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions Well first I have to admit, I do not have an internet saavy family. And this game is very much tied into internet memes from "I can haz cheezburgers?" to "Erhmahgerd." Luckily, I have spent a healthy amount of my life researching internet culture, but I ended up having to explain a lot of the cards to my kids.

But the reason I love this game is because of how engaged it kept the kids, and the amount of laughs that it produced. The selfies were ridiculous and caused laughter in itself and the cards played were even better. The game is pretty simple, pick a card from your hand to recreate in a selfie, then others play cards with scenarios that best fit your selfie. There are a lot of "Trying not to poop" type of cards so the humor is a little juvenile but perfect for keeping kids engaged.

Everyone willingly took their turns on the cell phone and everyone seemed to really enjoy the game. Scoring was pretty meaningless which was good. I was thinking that since the person taking the photo got to be the judge of who gets the point for the best caption that there would be hurt feelings and poorly awarded points, but the fun of the selfies and reading the cards trumped any controversy. Actually we ended without caring who scored points.

All in all this is a great ice breaking game.
text_fidelity_b: Selfie - The Game of Silly Expressions

QMAN Girls Building Blocks Toys Trendy Cosmetics Store Building Kit Girls Make-Up Shop Street-View Bricks Toy for Girls Age 6-12 and Up (348 Pieces) I tried three of these off-brand LEGO sets in the "street store" model series - the coffee house, the make-up store, and the hair salon. Each of the finished stores is too small for your minifigs to actually use, which is quite disappointing - this is a look-at model only - but also like those models, the final product is quite a winner. Smooth bricks cover every surface, so it doesn't even look like a LEGO set when finished.

The instructions are fine, but certainly not as clear as they would be if made by LEGO, who have a long history of writing the best manuals in the business. These will do, but are certainly not entirely clear.

The tilted coffee cup on the roof of the cafe really makes this one stand out, and it offers a lot of interesting pieces that make this one stand out. This is the clear winner of the three I tried, and if I only bought one, this would be it.

The make-up store and the hair salon were both good, but looked a lot more typical when finished. They are quite colorful, and have some unique aspects in the interior. These sets were fine, but slightly more difficult to build, and a little bit more finicky in terms of detail work. The final product is a lot less identifiable, but they still look good on the shelf, and have plenty in them that you can use in other models.

Thames & Kosmos Big Engineering Makerspace | Science Kit | 22 Physics Lessons & Experiments | Toy of The Year Award Finalist | Homeschool | Learning Pod | STEM Kit This THAMES & KOSMOS THE BIG ENGINEERING MAKERSPACE SCIENCE EXPERIMENT KIT is the real deal--a fun model-building kit that painlessly teaches basic concepts of physics (e.g., thermal air currents, levers, momentum). Each model (e.g., crane, helicopter) actually works, and is accompanied by a “what's happening here” explanation in the manual of why it works (e.g., turning a crank hoists a crane load by exerting force on a rope threaded through pulleys that share the weight to be lifted; a helicopter’s fast tail rotor produces a force that counteracts the main rotor’s force to stabilize the helicopter).

The models are assembled from plastic parts (some parts are similar to LEGO Technic elements) by following clear step-by-step diagrams (similar to LEGO building instructions). They are powered by a pressurized air tank controlled by a switch with a lever. There are no batteries to buy or charge, because you pressurize the air tank by pumping air into it (the pump assembly resembles a bicycle tire pump).

Each model has suggestions for finding out more about the scientific principles that relate to it. The manual indicates the difficulty level of each model with a three-dot system (easy, medium, difficult).

This kit may seem expensive (about $90 on Amazon), but it teaches a LOT about the practical application of physical and engineering principles, for the price of a single medium-sized LEGO Technic kit. It's a kit to use in home schooling, or to give to a child who really wants to understand why and how construction equipment, vehicles, watercraft, aircraft, and cameras work in the real world.
text_fidelity_b: Thames & Kosmos Big Engineering Makerspace | Science Kit | 22 Physics Lessons & Experiments | Toy of The Year Award Finalist | Homeschool | Learning Pod | STEM Kit

CTSC 75FT 95FT 110FT 250FT Zipline Kit with Stainless Steel Spring Brake and Seat My kids love this. I had a couple of trees a bit over a hundred feet apart on a shallow incline, which seemed pretty perfect.

I did end up putting this together and taking it apart about ten times before I was satisfied with it, so I definitely dumped more time than I intended into it. Making adjustments is often almost as big a job as starting from scratch. The loop at the top of the line was small, and that wanted to attach to a giant redwood, so I had to switch trees, though I'm sure I could've bought a longer section of cable. The bottom end seems like it would be able to handle a big tree fine. Maybe I could've swapped ends, but it doesn't indicate that as an option anywhere. The instructions are a bit sparse, but mostly sufficient. I hadn't realized initially that the big velcro pads had a slot for the cable to go through to keep it from slipping off the pad. By the time I got everything attached high enough, I had a lot of trouble pulling all of the slack out of the line. The turnbuckle was way too short for the task. I eventually had to get creative with clamps and bungee cords to get enough mechanical advantage to pull it tight enough to clamp it down.

The included seat is nice for when you want both adults and kids to be able to use it. It allows it to be attached up high enough to be out of the way and usable by adults, while still being low enough for smaller kids to ride on the seat. My kids use it more than the trampoline, so it's a hit.
text_fidelity_b: CTSC 75FT 95FT 110FT 250FT Zipline Kit with Stainless Steel Spring Brake and Seat

text_fidelity_a:
Harry Potter Hogwarts Battle Cooperative Deck Building Card Game | Official Harry Potter Licensed Merchandise | Harry Potter Board Game | Great Gift for Harry Potter Fans | Harry Potter Movie artwork Great fun. Nice cooperative game to play with others to avoid hurt feelings, players "out of the game", and to make things feel low-stakes and casual. You never really rely on others players, it's just that some players can help each other out when possible, but no one loses before anyone else. You all lose at once.

There aren't any story events from the books during each year. As you progress through years, your character cards swap out for older portraits and new enemies and spells are introduced, but your starting character spells never change. You always have to rebuild the deck and gain low level spells even in later years, which seems pretty silly. The strategy can be dumbed down after a while and it really just depends on who the starting villains you get dealt are. You could spend as long as you want building your deck if you get someone like Crabbe and Goyle in the first round.

Dont expect this to be story-rich or something. Seems to just be harry potter themed, in the sense that this could really be almost any other story or universe that has multiple books or a serialized progression and it would also have worked fine. They just happened to pick Harry Potter. That could be a good thing however, since you essentially need zero harry potter knowledge to play.
text_fidelity_b: Harry Potter Hogwarts Battle Cooperative Deck Building Card Game | Official Harry Potter Licensed Merchandise | Harry Potter Board Game | Great Gift for Harry Potter Fans | Harry Potter Movie artwork

Quadrilla Wooden Marble Run Construction - The Roundabout - Quality Time Playing Together Wooden Safe Play - Smart Play for Smart Families I was so glad I found this brand of marble maze. We have bought a few plastic versions but they have all been flimsy and not very engaging.

This marble maze series made by Hape is tremendous. We have had so much fun building with this. Not only does each set come with a book and great step by step directions with photos for making multiple mazes the color coded-functionality of the transporting blocks help kids work out marble flow and direction when building on their own. Some blocks allow marbles to flow one or two directions or alternating directions as well as some being travel though pieces while others are drop into pieces.

Although the wood pieces fit together they do not lock so it can be knocked over which may be an issue for younger children who get really excited like my four year old grandson but my seven year old son builds and maintains his mazes with no problems.

It also comes with a bag full or marbles so never having a marble should never be an issue. We use a funnel and just load the maze up and it can have a marble flow continuously for as long as someone collects and loads. It's a bundle of excitement and engages the kids for HOURS!

Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder These products, both the dry float lounger and the socializer are prime examples of why I test products the way I do prior to writing my review.

When I initially received these products and inflated them I was fairly impressed with the design and comfort - by 18 days later both were flat lumps of rubber in the trash.

First the socializer never held air. After inflation by the following morning it had deflated to around 70% capacity. I put it under water in the pool and discovered multiple small defects in 2 seams.

The dry float lounger lasted a bit longer at 18 days but then was found flat due to a separation at the seam.

It is important to note neither of these were ever used by children or in any rough play as when I review products I adhere to strict guidelines - and there are no children in the home.

While the socializer is listed as a dry float it appears the user’s calves and feet would be in the water. The lounger pool float is perfect for those who prefer to float completely out of the water. When floating on this no part of the body is submerged in the water.

While 88-90% of the world’s population is right handed this manufacturer chose to place the cup holder on the left side and made it too small to hold a standard 12 Oz can for both of these floats. This is simply poor designing.

While these floats come with a small patch kit, these are only helpful when repairing a puncture and absolutely will not hold a torn seam.

While these floats appeared to have promise initially, in well under a month they proved to be poorly designed, and of substandard construction and materials.

I would not recommend either of these products.
text_fidelity_b: Swimways Dry Float Lounger Pool Float, Translucent Inflatable Recliner Chair for Adults with Fast Inflation, Foot Rest & Cup Holder

He loved it when he opened it, "that's cool!" was the exact response.
-There was no assembly necessary.
-One battery pack was in the car and needed to be connected and the spare battery was in a separate box.
-The controller did require batteries (not included).
-There was a usb charging cable for the car battery packs, but there is no wall plug (so a wall plug or usb connectable device is needed).

The battery was fully charged in the car so we got to test it right away. Good thing is that we crashed several times but no cosmetic damages (fish tank stand, kitchen table, wall (twice), coffee table, my legs (yes, both).

The car was pretty fast but not as fast as I anticipated. That is probably a good thing for my 8 year old as the crashes like meant speed was about right for his first time using this car. His birthday was a few days ago and he's played with it for several minutes each day since then with no need to charge that battery (or use the secondary battery thus far).

The battery does say it will need 3 hours to charge though so BE READY to get that second battery on the charger right when you get this car.

Overall, very satisfied. It is a 4/5 for us and would get a 5/5 if the controller came with batteries and USB charger had a wall plug.

Klutz Sew Mini Treats Craft Kit, 8" Length x 1.5" Width x 9" Height We adore the Klutz art kits, especially the clay and eraser making kits. We had always passed on this one because it looks like it is a decent step harder than the others and we were right. It takes a lot more patience and hand eye coordination to sew a cute cartoon creation than it does to roll weird shaped balls of clay. But this kit is pretty nice. I would have given it five stars if it weren't for the clay and eraser kits which seemed easier and kept the kids engaged better.

The kit does have all you need to make some pretty adorable creations. Three of the four of us made donuts as our test creations and one tried the lemon. For the most part we made decent donuts, but the lemon looks a little more like a potsticker. We improved our stitching rather quickly, but I suspect our next creations will be considerably better. We did augment the set with a couple of additional sewing needles and some thread to give all four of us a chance to work at the same time. We also will be buying more felt. There is a decent amount in the kit for an introduction, but if it takes off we will quickly run out. (We did the same with bake clays for the clay kit.)

I hope this takes off for a couple of the kids because the end product is very cute.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Sew Mini Treats Craft Kit, 8" Length x 1.5" Width x 9" Height

text_fidelity_a:
Driven Recycling Truck Vehicle We absolutely adore this recycling truck! There is a little side area that opens up to hold the trashcan and a broom, you can open the trash truck from two different areas to add trash, mush the trash, etc., and the opportunities for varied play are endless. What we like to do in our house is use tissue from gifting, tear it into little pieces and then crunch it into little balls, which are then moved with a front loader into the recycling truck directly, or onto a small conveyor belt that we have that loads the trash that way. It is a really fun set up and has provided seriously countless hours of fun for my kids ages 3 to 5. There is some light and sound that happens when you push the buttons, but it's realistic light and sound and not obnoxious or excessive.

Overall I can't overstate how much we love this vehicle, as well as the other trucks from this brand. We have some more expensive ones, but these are absolutely is good in terms of the play value and the quality level. We haven't broken any of our driven trucks yet, and that is saying something given how much they are used.
text_fidelity_b: Driven Recycling Truck Vehicle

text_fidelity_a:
Baby Alive Happy Hungry Baby Brown Straight Hair Doll, Makes 50+ Sounds & Phrases, Eats & Poops, Drinks & Wets, for Kids Age 3 & Up Returning again. But this time to manufacturer.

Adorable doll. Super cute voice, movements, interactions. 9yo received as gift from Santa (has been asking for a baby alive for no less than four years). She opened and played with it once the day after Christmas, then “put it to bed fresh and clean”. The next day, it did not work. We had figured it was because she did use it for two hours the first day- guessed that the store batteries died. We replaced the batteries with brand new Duracell‘s… Nothing. It still did not work. Through her tears from disappointment, and a quick explanation that Santa needs help after Xmas (because why would Santa send a toy that would break!?) We utilized Kohls return to Amazon.
We received the replacement doll yesterday. Same exact doll. Again she played with it for two hours- under the close supervision of myself to ensure she was following the directions. She put it to bed fresh and clean, and at 8 o’clock this morning she came into my room crying that it’s not working. We tried new batteries, switch placements, pressing and holding the belly. Nothing.
I called Hasbro this morning and they are sending a return label, and a different replacement baby alive doll.
Overall I’m extremely disappointed in this product. I was unable to find anyone else having the same issue. I highly doubt it is result of my daughter playing. This is designed for children ages three and up. She is a nine-year-old who is extremely cautious. This was her only Santa gift and it has caused lots of heartache. We do our best to downplay the frustration. We understand malfunctions happen. I just don’t want anybody else to have the same issue and feel alone like we did.
I would not recommend this doll specifically. Fingers crossed the third replacement (A different design) works more than once.

Update: we purchased a 3rd replacement happy hungry baby from a local store. A different hair color than our first two. Hoping it’s a different production line. It’s still working on day two! My daughter squealed this morning with excitement “she works! She works!”

Shes used the 3rd happy hungry baby (brunette) for weeks now- almost daily. Its been working wonderfully! Still unbelievable that the first two were defective (Black hair). Raised to 2 stars for the fact she loves it. The headache and hassle of 2 dolls would make it where i would -cautiously- recommend. Keep the box (and receipt) for at least a month.
text_fidelity_b: Baby Alive Happy Hungry Baby Brown Straight Hair Doll, Makes 50+ Sounds & Phrases, Eats & Poops, Drinks & Wets, for Kids Age 3 & Up

text_fidelity_a:
Winning Moves Games Classic Twister Ah, the memories I have from playing Twister when I was 16 and drove a red Firebird. Paul, who I wished was my boyfriend was interested in me only as a friend, so the best way I had to get close to him was to invite friends over for a game of Twister. Memories are interesting because I recall exactly what he and I were both wearing -- he in a light blue oxford Gant shirt and me in my self designed and sewn striped wide legged hip-hugger slacks, solid shirt and matching striped vest. I can't tell you who else was there, but we had a full house and we had a blast with my little sister calling our moves and tattling when we were having TOO much fun.

[[ASIN:B00HVTH2MC Classic Twister]] can be played by most ages, provided the bodies are somewhat agile and the individuals are not really shy. The vinyl mat allows for between 2 and 4 people, no more. A game lasts less than 15 minutes usually with the winner being the person who remains on the mat without falling over. A designated person who is not on the mat spins the little plastic on cardboard wheel and those playing place the appropriate limb on a designated spot. For color blind people, your friends will let you know where to put that foot or hand, I guarantee. It is a really fun physical game that stimulates conversation and breaks the ice. I noticed that there are several versions of the game available as of today but cannot tell you what the differences are or why the prices vary. What I can tell you is that this is a really amusing game for all ages, even those who can't actually do the moving but can participate from the peanut gallery.
text_fidelity_b: Winning Moves Games Classic Twister

I have four kids, and they like science very much. This has a lot of different projects that showcase different principles of science and chemistry.

The experiments are not too hard to do. In our case, a parent did it with the kids. When chemicals are involved, I would recommend adult supervision.

The kids really enjoyed doing it. I like that after the experiments you can talk about how and why it happened. It really can foster an interest in science.

A lot came with it, but you do need some of your own supplies. Most you probably already had. While I wish everything was included, just about every similar kit on the market is like this, so I didn't take off any stars for it.

Overall, this is fun and educational. I also like giving these sorts of things as gifts because parents appreciate them.
